An unauthenticated remote attacker can exhaust server memory and CPU by sending a request body composed of many tiny 1-byte chunks, because the reader stores each chunk separately and no limit is applied to chunk count.

It is not yet KEV-listed and has a very low EPSS score, but defenders running affected services should watch for a fix and consider limiting request bodies.

events.why_it_matters: Both vulnerabilities carry a CNA-assigned CVSS score of 8.7, and because Bandit is a server library, applications accepting HTTP/2 request bodies could be kept hanging by cheap, unauthenticated traffic. Neither CVE is listed in KEV and EPSS scores are low, suggesting no confirmed mass exploitation yet, but defenders running affected software should track the developing status for a patch.
